images.title: Turns that look the same
images.purpose: Show a ceiling fan, a flower and a wheel that each look the same after a turn smaller than a full turn.
images.composition: Three objects in one row with wide space between and a label below each.
images.exact_structure: Left: a fan of 3 equal teal #0072B2 blades from a centre dot. Middle: a flower of 5 equal amber #E69F00 petals around a centre dot. Right: a wheel with 8 equal spokes in grey #6B7280 inside a ring and a hub. Each has a small reddish purple #CC79A7 curved arrow for its smallest turn. Exactly 3 objects with 3, 5 and 8 equal parts.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: An object has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a turn less than a full turn.
images.description: A three bladed fan, a five petal flower and an eight spoke wheel, each with its smallest turn: 120, 72 and 45 degrees.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many equal parts each object has and how big its smallest turn is.

image_decisions.why: Three examples of rotational symmetry are a picture idea; one clean image carries them.
